text.p: Malaysia's Promet Bhd said on Friday that it is re-selling a 32.9 percent stake acquired late last year in maritime engineering firm Westmont Industries Bhd to unlisted Swascojuta Sdn Bhd.
In a statement, Promet said the decision followed the cancellation of a proposal to sell its entire equity stake in its Promet Fabricators Sdn Bhd unit and four pieces of land to Westmont Industries.
The disposals would have helped fund the Westmont stake acquisition.
Promet in December had said the deal with Westmont was part of a group restructuring which would have seen Promet's maritime engineering activities injected into Westmont.

But because the deals on the land and fabricator unit shares have been called off, Promet's board "has agreed to un-wind the acquisition" of 76.7 million shares representing 32.9 percent equity interest in Westmont Industries, the statement said.
No reason was provided for the cancelled disposals.
The sale of the stake in Westmont Industries will not have a material effect on Promet's net tangible assets or its earnings, the statement said.
In November, Promet had said it would spend "close to half a billion ringgit" to buy the Westmont stake from unlisted Westmont Holdings Sdn Bhd.

News of the stake purchase was embroiled in controversy when Westmont Land (Asia) Bhd, a property developer and affiliate company of Westmont Industries, said in December that it was also buying the 32.9 percent stake in Westmont Industries.
Westmont Land said in a statement in December that it was considering legal redress over the sale of the stake to Promet.
Both Westmont Land and Westmont Industries are controlled by tycoon Joseph Chong.
